To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) patients with normal pressure (NPH) who responded to shunt operation showed reduced cerebral blood flow and cerebrovascular reserve capacity, (2) patients with NPH, who did not respond, showed normal cerebrovascular reserve but reduced cerebral blood flow, and (3) patients with ventricomegaly without NPH showed normal cerebral blood flow but reduced cerebrovascular reserve.

(a) CBF is reduced in symptomatic patients with NPH after SAH due, in part, to impaired CVR; (b) CVR is reduced in asymptomatic patients after SAH with hydrocephalus; and (c) CBF is not necessarily decreased in asymptomatic patients.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the cerebral circulation in patients with ventriculo-megaly after SAH and with the mechanism of NPP.
the pathophysiology of normal pressure hydrocephaly (NPH) in patients with ventricular enlargement after subarachoid haemorrhages (SAH).
the pathophysiology of hydrocephalus after aneurysmal SAH.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanism responsible for NPH is a combination of reduced CBF and impaired CVR.
CBF is reduced in symptomatic patients with NPH, but that CVR is reduced in both symptomatic and asymptomic patients with ventricolomegaly after subarachnoi haemorrhage.
patients with NPH after SAH due a ruptured aneurism have impaired CVR and reduced CBF.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CBF is not reduced in asymptomatic patients, but that CVR may be impaired.
the mechanism of NHP is not a simple impairment of CVR, but rather a reduction of CBF super-imposed on the pre-existing impairment of the CVR.
the mechanism of the symptoms of NPH after SAH is the superimposition of CBF reduction on the pre-existing impairment of cerebrovascular reactivities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cerebral blood flow and CVR are reduced in patients with hydrocephaulus after subarachnoi haemorrhage and that these reductions may be related to the symptoms of normal pressure hydrocephulus (NPH).
the reduction of cerebral blood flow and cerebrovascular reserve capacity may be an essential factor in the mechanism responsible of the symptoms in patients with normal-pressure hydrocephalus.
patients with ventriculo-megaly after SAH may be divided into three groups: patients with NPH (group A), patients without NPH (group B) and patients without NPH who have symptoms of NPH (group C).
